original_question.anatomical_scope: Human physiology is the motivating frame, but these fragments concern cell-culture and preclinical dental-repair experiments. The paper-level species, tissues, compartments and conditions require primary-source verification.
original_question.species_and_system_scope: F02 archive claim: mammalian cell cultures expressing/testing human cryptochrome in a pulsed-field experiment; exact cell line and preparations are not confirmed here. F03 archive claim: dental stem-cell and animal dentin-regeneration preclinical systems; animal species, model details and exact preparation require paper review. Neither should be described as a human intervention on this record.
original_question.observable_and_timescale: The archive describes changes in ROS and ROS associated with light/TGF-β1 activation but supplies no chemical-species-resolved observable, units, assay protocol, time course, or repeated-measure design. These remain unknown; no stochastic model is justified from the available record.
original_question.discriminating_observation: Compare the named probes/assays and controls in the original methods and supplements, their sampling compartment and time after exposure, then test whether the same chemically identified species is necessary in both systems. A generic ROS signal alone cannot distinguish that proposition.

physiology.human_anchor: No specific human organ-level process has been established by the material reviewed in this session. F03 concerns dental repair models, but the archive's summary does not identify which cells or animal species in each experiment.
physiology.cross_site_transfer: Not established. Do not infer a body-wide or tissue-to-tissue ROS signal from either fragment.

interpretation.conclusion: The shared archive label 'ROS' presently connects two different experimental questions: a pulsed-field-associated intracellular response in cell cultures (F02) and light-associated signaling in dental-repair models (F03). With no source-verified assay identity, it does not establish that the same chemical species, compartment, timescale or mechanism is involved.
